courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces AI vocabulary, capabilities, limitations and applications in nontechnical terms.

courses.name: Artificial Intelligence Applications
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Builds AI applications with low-code or no-code tools, language-model workflows, retrieval and agents; team projects evaluate performance, cost and responsible use.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: [COP 2510 (min grade B) OR CGS 2060 (min grade B)] AND CAI 1000 (min grade B)

courses.name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces AI methods and software for search, reasoning and learning, including basic machine learning.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: COP 3514 (min grade B) AND CDA 3103 (min grade B); Co-prerequisites: COP 4530; Course restrictions: Majors Only

courses.name: Ethical Issues in Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Examines professional and ethical responsibilities in AI through developing and presenting responses to real-world problems.

courses.name: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Surveys supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement and deep learning, emphasizing evaluation and responsible practice.

courses.name: Deep Learning
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Covers neural-network mathematics, single- and multilayer models, applications and ethical concerns.

courses.name: AI System Architecture and Infrastructure
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Studies AI training/deployment infrastructure, frameworks, data pipelines, distributed systems and cloud scaling through practical system design.
courses.prerequisites: Prerequisites: CDA 3103 (min grade B) AND CAI 4002 (min grade C)

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.description: 2026–2027 public course inventory: Introduces image formation and segmentation, feature matching, shape and texture analysis, object recognition and changing scenes.

requirements.title: General education and unrestricted electives
requirements.summary: Brochure lists state natural science and humanities, USF humanities and social sciences, and unrestricted electives. Approved pools and overlap rules remain unreviewed.

requirements.title: Advising and optional experiences
requirements.summary: Sequence is recommended for full-time students. Students not calculus-ready can start with precalculus with advising. Summer research, abroad and internship experiences are recommendations, not mandatory courses.

requirements.title: University minimum degree credits
requirements.summary: Registrar overview gives 120 credit hours for this university requirement; program-specific requirements may be stricter. The normalized unit and detailed applicability remain unverified.

requirements.title: University minimum upper-level credits
requirements.summary: Registrar overview gives 42 credit hours for this university requirement; program-specific requirements may be stricter. The normalized unit and detailed applicability remain unverified.

requirements.title: Published summer-enrollment minimum
requirements.summary: Registrar overview gives 9 credit hours for this university requirement; program-specific requirements may be stricter. The normalized unit and detailed applicability remain unverified. The registrar FAQ permits documented waiver requests; entry-cohort exceptions remain unresolved.

requirements.title: University final-credit residency
requirements.summary: Complete 30 of the final 60 credit hours at USF according to the registrar overview. Additional major/college residency requirements remain unverified.

requirements.title: Conditional summer-enrollment waiver
requirements.summary: A waiver may be requested for documented seasonal summer employment in each summer missed, unavailable program courses certified by an advisor, or exceptional hardship outside the student’s control. Submit supporting evidence during the graduation-application semester; allow three weeks for a decision. A request is not automatic approval.

requirements.title: Grade-forgiveness limits
requirements.summary: Both attempts must be at USF; the repeat grade must be at least D. At most three forgiveness uses are allowed, with one repeat per course. Academic-dishonesty FF grades are excluded, and forgiveness cannot change courses counted toward an already awarded bachelor’s degree. This does not establish AI-major passing grades.

requirements.title: General education: 36 published credit hours
requirements.summary: Complete 15 state-core and 21 USF-designated credit hours across five disciplines, including the additional two-course choice below. Current approved course attributes determine eligibility; no finite pool is inferred.

requirements.title: Communication
requirements.summary: Three state-core credits plus three USF-designated credits in this discipline; choose currently approved courses. Credit unit normalization remains unverified.

requirements.title: Two further general-education courses
requirements.summary: Choose two courses totaling six published credits from any of the five general-education disciplines.

requirements.title: Enhancement and state-core reuse rules
requirements.summary: Enhancement labels impose no separate student quota. A state-core course may sometimes serve as a general-education elective; an advisor must confirm the major-specific use. This does not authorize double-counting one course in two slots.

requirements.title: Current course-attribute approval
requirements.summary: Use the public Course Inventory and filter Course Attributes by the required general-education discipline. Approval is a current designation; the full changing pool is not invented from brochure examples.

requirements.title: Civic-literacy entry cohorts
requirements.summary: Complete applicable civic literacy before graduation. The entry date at a Florida public institution controls: before Summer B 2018 generally exempt; Summer B 2018–Summer A 2021 requires course or assessment; Summer B 2021 onward requires both. Out-of-state and additional-degree students are not categorically exempt; the FAQ requires returning earlier graduates to fulfill previously unmet civic literacy.

requirements.title: Approved course and assessment routes
requirements.summary: Course options are POS 2041, AMH 2020, AMH 2010 completed Fall 2024 onward, or transfer-only AMS X010 from Fall 2024 onward. Assessment uses FCLE or approved acceleration. The internal USF Canvas test is available only to pre-Fall-2024 entrants and requires 60%, with unlimited attempts.

requirements.title: Civic transfer and prior assessment evidence
requirements.summary: Florida public-college/university credit needs official transcript evidence for each completed component; an incomplete component remains due. A high-school FCLE pass of at least 60% needs the official transcript and satisfies assessment only. Out-of-state course substitutions require an advisor-submitted syllabus review.

requirements.title: General-education overlap and passing grade
requirements.summary: POS X041, AMH X010 and AMH X020 may also meet state-core social science with C− or better. A lower passing grade may satisfy civic literacy alone. AMH X010 must be completed Fall 2024 onward. Naturalization testing does not satisfy the assessment.

requirements.title: Approved acceleration mechanisms
requirements.summary: Both components: AP US Government ≥3, AP US History ≥4, CLEP American Government ≥50, or CLEP US History I ≥50. Course only: AICE US History A-level A–E, CLEP US History II ≥50, IB History of the Americas 5–7, or passing approved dual enrollment (Fall 2024 timing applies to AMH X010/AMS X010).

requirements.title: Statewide course-equivalency framework
requirements.summary: SCNS equivalence ordinarily requires the same prefix/last three digits, comparable faculty credentials and the applicable minimum grade; equivalent transferred work serves requirements on the same basis as native credit. Quarter and semester amounts may differ. Other credit acceptance remains institution-specific.

requirements.title: Exceptions to automatic course equivalency
requirements.summary: Individual review applies to unoffered or unaccredited/pre-transfer-date courses; 900–999 special work; adult applied academics; graduate courses; internships, apprenticeships, practica, clinical or abroad experiences; and performing-art/Criminal Justice skill courses. These exceptions do not establish approval for an AI requirement.
